summary: Melee Survival with a Tallstrider, built around Expose Prey into Mongoose Bite. The Tallstrider's Dust Cloud fills the minor armor slot when no druid or warlock does.
rotation: Pre-pull: walk into melee at -6s, Aspect of the Beast at -3s, Hunter's Mark at -1.5s
Racials, potions and other cooldowns as soon as they're ready
Hunter's Mark (rank 4, +143 ranged attack power) at -1.5s, recast in its last 3s. The raid's mark is off
Mongoose Bite whenever Expose Prey or a dodge enables it
Immolation Trap on cooldown at 30%+ mana
Raptor Strike queued on the next swing when it's ready
Lacerate when it's down, at 20%+ mana
Wing Clip on free GCDs at 50%+ mana, but not when an enabled Mongoose Bite is about ready
The Tallstrider (1.0s) bites on cooldown, and keeps Dust Cloud (505 armor, 30s, 10 focus) on the boss while no Faerie Fire or Curse of Recklessness holds the minor armor slot
consumes: Dense Sharpening Stone (main hand and off hand)
caveats: The Tallstrider costs 41.1 DPS at 180s against the same build without it (987.8 against 1028.9, 20,000 iterations, seed 1). The search weighs that against what the pet gives the raid.

A Tallstrider has Bite, Dash and Dust Cloud and no Claw, so it does less damage than the cat. This request keeps the raid's Faerie Fire and Curse of Recklessness, so it never casts Dust Cloud: the number is the pet's cost. The raid sim switches them off when nobody gives them, and the pet then keeps Dust Cloud up itself.
The Tallstrider keeps the cat's 1.0s swing (Faster Attack VII) and Cobra Reflexes. Its hits scale with the speed, so a slower one changes little.
The pet gets 10% of the hunter's ranged attack power on top of its own 254, plus the hunter's crit and hit (from beta pet sheets).
Assumed: Raptor Strike rank 8 adds 96, halfway between the client and Era.
Left out: Fire-toasted Bun (+9, seasonal) and Elemental Sharpening Stone (Molten Core plans).
Crit per Agility is Classic's level 60 rate (0.0189% per point), from Forever's game files.
Pet hits scale with attack speed, as seen on a level 17 pet. A 1.0s raptor would add about 2 DPS (Savage Rend), but none that fast is known.
Survival never shoots, so the ranged weapon doesn't matter.
Immolation Trap adds 10% of ranged attack power over its whole duration. This is from Blizzard's notes, not checked in a log.
Assumed: each hunter keeps up its own Hunter's Mark, and the raid's mark is off. That costs 0.5 to 2.5 DPS at 180s (1.5 here).

No Scorpid Sting. Balance druids already keep up Insect Swarm, which gives the same 2% hit reduction. On a ranged hunter, Scorpid Sting would replace Serpent Sting and cost about 85 to 100 DPS for nothing.
